column1: # Defects a subplan knowingly shipped, and the checkpoint that owns resolving them.
# Read by test/guards/carrieddefects_test.go. A subplan that finds a defect it may not fix — because
# fixing it would change another subplan's frozen contract, or would exceed its own scope — records
# it here instead of in a commit body, where nothing enforces it. The guard makes the row load-
#   - Every UNRESOLVED row must name a live evidence test, so the defect cannot be silently fixed
#     and left recorded as broken, nor recorded and left unpinned.
#   - Every id must have a section in the detail document, so "what is this" always has an answer.
#   - No unresolved row may survive its RESOLVER's completion report. That is the gate: a wave
#     cannot be signed off with rows it was responsible for.
# `open` and `deferred:<checkpoint>` are both unresolved; only `fixed` and `wontfix` are not. A
# deferral names the LATER checkpoint that must dispose of the row, that checkpoint must have a
# plans/<checkpoint>-*.md document, and the row then blocks ITS report rather than its owner's.
#   id        stable identifier, <subplan>-D<n>, referenced from code comments and tests
#   opened_by the subplan that shipped the defect
#   owner     the checkpoint that must resolve or consciously re-defer it
#   evidence  test that pins the current behaviour, or "-" for rows with no runtime symptom
#   summary   one line, present tense, describing what is wrong
# Resolving a row means EITHER fixing the defect and setting status to `fixed`, OR setting it to
# `deferred:<later-checkpoint>` and adding the reason to the detail document. Both are conscious
# acts recorded in git history; neither can be reached by doing nothing.

column6: JSON-escaped Windows temp paths are not canonicalized, so they fork the dedup space and carry user names into stored content
canonicalization is not idempotent when a deletion joins two fragments into a value neither half contained
one timestamp edge remains of the original three: a word byte after an ISO timestamp defeats the rule, and fixing it is legal only under fixed-point composition, so it travels with SP04-D2
devtool cover's landedSubplans must gain SP-02 and SP-03 at the wave-1 merge or their coverage floors stay off
canonicalization cost is now dominated by per-rule prefilter scans, so each new rule spends the hot-path budget linearly
BenchmarkRun_Bash100KB measured +-33% run to run on the reference host, which the 25% bench-compare threshold cannot distinguish from a regression

GCPolicy.Deadline binds the mark's hash harvest and the sweep, but tombstoneDeadRoots and the mark's index walks answer only to ctx, so GCReport.Duration can overshoot the deadline by the whole tombstone phase (100-260 ms measured at 650 dead roots)

a drain aborted by idle-budget expiry consumes the line it interrupted (offset advanced and seen-set committed before the binding completed), losing the event; the deliberate poison-line consume rule does not distinguish a dying drain from a refusing handler
the synthetic corpus raises only DemandFileContent, so tool_edit_distance, re_attempts and decision_preservation are measured over an input that cannot exercise them
file_set_jaccard is pinned at 1.0: the only repair re-reads the path key the demanding turn already touches, so the repaired set is the demanded set by construction
the Belady keep budget never binds on the corpus (oracle rewrite_span_tokens is 0 at every event), so fraction_of_opt grades against a trivial ceiling
belady.pMin iterates candidates where 5.2 defines it over all blocks; the deviation is recorded only in a code comment
decision_preservation measures post-compaction horizon agreement, which deterministic mode fixes at 1.0, not 11.2's pre-compaction decisions still recalled
the stock model skips the 4/3 host padding: hostPadTokens has no production caller and hostSkillBudget is dead
canon.Decide has no consumer and 8.1's delta-vs-full storage write is implemented nowhere and owned by nobody
the PutBytes cold and warm budgets (3 ms / 400 us) are 9x and 19x over on Windows and have never been measured on the reference platform

OnToolUse over a 256 KB tool result breaches budget B-C (l0_process, p99 < 50 ms): 53-115 ms on Qompack.md 8.1's own one-changed-line case and 262-655 ms when every chunk is novel, dominated by store.PutBytes's per-novel-chunk object-write path
